questions.text:
Consider the following table


The table is in which normal form?
questions.solution:
From the diagram: AB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] C, D, E and C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B.

- Candidate keys: AB and AC, so A, B, C are prime.
- No partial or transitive dependency of a non-prime attribute [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3NF.
- C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B has C not a super key [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not BCNF. (It is allowed in 3NF because B is prime.)

Answer: Third Normal Form but not BCNF

questions.text: Let x, y, z, a, b, c be the attributes of an entity set E. If {x}, {x,y}, {a,b}, {a,b,c}, {x,y,z} are superkeys then which of the following are the candidate keys?
questions.solution:
A candidate key is a minimal super key.

- {x} is minimal, so {x, y} and {x, y, z} are not candidate keys.
- {a, b} is minimal (nothing smaller is listed), so {a, b, c} is not.

Answer: {x} and {a, b}

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Every time the attribute A appears, it is matched with the same value of attribute B but not the same value of attribute C. Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
A always comes with the same B [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] functional dependency A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B.

A can come with many values of C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] multivalued dependency A [latex]\twoheadrightarrow[/latex] C.

Answer: A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B, A [latex]\twoheadrightarrow[/latex] C

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Consider the schema [latex]R(A,B,C,D)[/latex] and the functional dependencies [latex]A \rightarrow B[/latex] and [latex]C \rightarrow D[/latex].  If the decomposition is made as [latex]R_{1}(A, B)[/latex] and [latex]R_{2}(C, D)[/latex], then which of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B lies in R1 and C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] D in R2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] dependency preserving.
- [latex]R_1\cap R_2=\emptyset[/latex], which is not a key of either part [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] lossy join.

Answer: Preserves dependency but cannot perform lossless join

questions.text: An aggregation association is drawn using which symbol?
questions.solution:
In UML, aggregation is drawn with a hollow (open) diamond at the whole end. A filled (closed) diamond means composition.

Answer: A small open diamond at the end of a line connecting two tables

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: A line which loops back on to the same table
A small open diamond at the end of a line connecting two tables
A small closed diamond at the end of a line connecting two tables
A small closed triangle at the end of a line connecting two tables
